_comment: Rules for server.mjs (hot-reloaded on the next request after this file changes; a broken file is logged and the previous rules stay active).

Source: the 203->153 rewrite spec of 2026-11-04 (builds mw main.7350e9b0198f982a848a.js, ui main.38358e33.js, ui 4555.dd346277.chunk.js). README.md explains every rule, what is kept on purpose and the optional rewrites that are NOT applied.

backend: '203-mac' (default) serves /synapse/products/153/** from the Mac 203 (Basilisk V3 35K) module with rewrites; '153-win' serves Razer's Windows 153 module from apps.razer.com (untested fallback). Override without editing: MIRROR_BACKEND=153-win or --backend 153-win.
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by the server.

jsonEdits.name: dashboard-available-add-153
jsonEdits._why: Gate 1. No repId: background-manager would then report and open the module under the repId pid, and the 203 module never reads realProductId.

jsonEdits.name: win153-installer-manifest-add-osx
jsonEdits._why: The Windows installer-manifest has no 'osx' block; ResourceUpdateChecker on macOS reads res.osx.latest (TypeError, install status never resolves) and then fetches /<baseURL>/osx/<latest.url>. Copy of the 203 Mac osx block.

routes.name: lighting-manifest-153
routes._why: Both backends. The lighting-engine first asks the module-local path; serve Razer's genuine DeviceManifest_153_<ed>.json (same ledConfig as 203: 1x11 device matrix, 7x5 chroma matrix) unmodified. Must precede the generic product routes.

routes.name: win153-osx-resource-manifest
routes._why: Answers the request that the injected osx block causes (/synapse/products/153/mw/manifests/osx/manifest-1.0.1.json) with the 203 Mac osx resource manifest (resources: [], no driver on macOS). Must precede module-153-from-win.

pathRewrite.name: 153_-segments-to-203_
pathRewrite._why: /synapse/products/153/ui/153_<ed>/PluginImages/153_<ed>_<layout>_dashboard1x.avif and /153_<ed>/dashboardNames.json exist upstream only under 203_ names. Example: .../153/ui/153_0/PluginImages/153_0_0_dashboard3x.avif -> .../203/ui/203_0/PluginImages/203_0_0_dashboard3x.avif.

rewrite.name: productId
rewrite._why: THE gate: DeviceInfo.productId, DEVICE_BASE_LOCAL_DATA.productId and the runtime default. connectCurrentDevice keeps devices whose productId is in [DeviceInfo.productId, bleId, dongleId]; connectHidDevice filters hid.getDevices() by productId. 'required': a main bundle without this literal is refused (502) instead of served as a module that can never find the mouse.

rewrite.name: webpack-context-keys
rewrite._why: Context keys built from the pid at runtime: mw ./${PID}_${ed}/translations, ui ./${pid}_${ed}/img_prods/*.png (synchronous require in TopViewComponent, throws without the 153 key).

rewrite.name: sw-precache-dirs
rewrite._why: Absolute precache URLs (PluginImages avif, dashboardNames.json) in the ui service worker.

rewrite.name: sw-precache-image-names
rewrite._why: File-name part of the two precached dashboard images.

rewrite.name: maxDPI
rewrite._why: Focus+ 26K sensor. Kept: mw 'd=35e3' (calibration constant) and ui 4967 'maxDPI||35e3' (fallback when maxDPI is falsy).

routes.name: module-153-from-win
routes._why: Razer's Windows 153 module (Daria_MW, master-m16-beta), same path, no text rewrites. Fallback only; untested at runtime.

routes.name: win153-razer-config
routes._why: 403 on apps-mac; the Windows mw main reads the global RazerConfig at top level.

routes.name: win153-rz-accessibility
routes._why: 403 on apps-mac, referenced by the Windows bundles. Checked 2026-11-04: these two are the only /synapse/assets/** paths the Windows 153 module references that apps-mac refuses.
